r.정치 구도: Peru has a presidential system, but Congress can remove a president fairly easily on grounds of 'moral incapacity,' which makes power unstable. The presidency has changed hands many times in the decade since 2016: in 2022 a president who tried to dissolve Congress was impeached and arrested, and in October 2025 Congress again ousted the president, citing rising crime. Congress, unicameral under the 1993 constitution, returned to two chambers with the 2026 elections, a 60-seat Senate and a 130-seat Chamber of Deputies. The June 2026 presidential runoff was decided by fewer than 50,000 votes, and the losing side refused to accept the result. Wide gaps in income and political leanings separate Lima from the Andean highlands and the Amazon, and a fragmented party system keeps Congress and the presidency in repeated conflict.

t.why: Alongside Chile and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, it is one of the world's top copper producers, a status that has grown more valuable in the era of electric vehicles and power-grid expansion. In November 2024 the port of Chancay, majority-owned by the Chinese state shipping group COSCO, opened and shortened sea routes between South America and Asia, while the United States has voiced concern about China's growing influence in the region. Peru hosted the APEC leaders' summit in Lima in 2024, is a founding member of the Pacific Alliance and belongs to the CPTPP trade pact. As the world's second-largest grower of coca after Colombia, drug enforcement is a major theme of its international cooperation. The memory of the 20-year conflict with the Maoist Shining Path, which began in 1980 and left about 70,000 dead, still weighs heavily on its politics.
t.rel: It settled border disputes with Chile through an international ruling and with Ecuador through a 1998 peace deal. The Chinese-built port of Chancay opened in 2024, becoming a gateway for trade with Asia.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1963, and their free trade agreement took effect in 2011, making Peru the second South American country after Chile to sign one with South Korea. KT-1 trainer aircraft from Korea Aerospace Industries were co-produced in Peru and delivered to the Peruvian Air Force in the 2010s. In December 2025 Hyundai Rotem signed a framework agreement with the Peruvian Army's arms factory to supply K2 tanks and wheeled armored vehicles. Defense cooperation built on local production and technology transfer is becoming a new pillar of the relationship.
t.know: Machu Picchu, built on a mountaintop by the Inca Empire in the 15th century, only became widely known to the outside world in 1911.
etext: The Andes hold rich deposits of copper, gold, silver and zinc, making mining the backbone of the economy. But protests and road blockades by communities near mines often halt output, and illegal gold mining is ravaging Amazon forests and rivers.

Water from the Andes has been channeled into the nearly rainless Pacific coastal desert to create large irrigated farms. As a result, Peru has become a farm-export powerhouse, selling blueberries, avocados and grapes while the Northern Hemisphere is in winter.

Despite frequent changes of president, the central bank has guarded its independence and kept inflation low. Public debt is also lower than in neighboring countries, so the currency has stayed relatively stable through political turmoil.

Around 70% of workers are in the informal sector, outside the tax and social insurance systems. State oil company Petroperú has needed repeated government bailouts, a sign of weak management of state firms, and rising extortion by criminal gangs has driven shopkeepers and transport workers to strike.
